verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both operator identities of (6.4) are stated exactly, as theorems rather than as notation: timeOp_expanded is 𝔱 = ∂_t + v_t·∂_Y and radialOp_expanded is 𝔯 = ∂_r + d r^{d−1}(v_r·∂_Y), with radialSpeed d r = d·r^{d−1} supplying the coefficient d_r r^{d_r−1} verbatim. The rewriting is only that the dot products N_abs = v_t·∂_Y and L_abs = v_r·∂_Y have no declarations of their own: they appear expanded into components, v.1 ∂_{Y₁} + v.2 ∂_{Y₂}, which is auxiliary_directional_eq. The Lean statements are for arbitrary d, vr, vt (not only the (6.2) data). The paper's remark that ∂_t and ∂_r hold Y fixed, and that 𝔱 and 𝔯 are physical differentiation before restriction, is partialT_pullback and partialR_pullback; partialR_pullback additionally needs r ≠ 0, which the paper's annulus supplies.
